notes: Nicia admission-decision-eval (Apache-2.0 repo with raw per-case results): a production-shaped task (decide whether an agent knowledge-base write needs human review) on 85 synthetic cases across six fictional organizations. First look 2026-10-01 (Jev, Clef, Clef-flash, Kev over public HTTPS from one US-west laptop between 21:30 UTC 2026-10-01 and 03:10 UTC 2026-10-02; Kev-27B on one Modal GPU; Kev-9B/4B via MLX on an Apple M4 Pro), hosted re-run 2026-10-04, GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI Decisions, public beta) 2026-10-06 from a cloud executor through an HTTPS proxy, region not recorded. Question wording and thresholds were tuned on Jev, not on Clef or Kev (a bias toward Jev). Latency ranges across passes are in claims, not rows (ranges, and the Luna latency is not a controlled comparison with the laptop runs). One case moves recall by 0.02: treat small gaps as noise.

claims.statement: Nicia latency as the caller sees it (one request at a time, p50 / p95; ranges are across passes): Jev 1.13.0 98-167 ms / 156-260 ms (re-run 2026-10-04 92-94 / 126-138); GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI Decisions, 2026-10-06, different environment) 168-171 / 277-284 ms; Kev-27B on one Modal container 255-263 / 318-479 ms; Clef-flash 429-533 / 677-732 ms (re-run 229-281 / 526-543); Clef 638-717 ms / 0.9-1.1 s (re-run 628-668 / 927 ms-1.1 s). With six requests in flight a single Kev container queued to 0.93-1.6 s p50. Hosted Clef from a laptop was about 4-7x slower than hosted Jev here, the opposite of the Cloudflare launch ratio; Nicia notes REST overhead of about 80 ms and that calling Clef through the Workers AI binding from inside a Worker was not measured.
claims.implication: Public-HTTPS caller latency to Workers AI is NOT what Cloudflare's on-platform figure means; measure from the Worker binding if you can.

claims.statement: Nicia: hosted Clef endpoints had a slow tail on 2026-10-01: several calls took 9 to 26 seconds and two of nine over-2.5 s calls never returned within 60 s; a few hours after launch about a fifth of Clef calls at six in flight returned 429 "Capacity temporarily exceeded". On 2026-10-04 Clef and Clef-flash returned exactly the same probabilities as on 2026-10-01 and the tail was gone (Clef-flash about twice as fast; no call failed or hung).

Nicia determinism: Jev is not deterministic (identical requests moved by up to 0.12 between passes, reordering up to 0.27; neither changed a decision in these runs); Kev-27B moved by at most 0.02 between identical requests and 0.11 under reordering; Clef is deterministic (identical requests returned identical probabilities) but order-sensitive: in its one miss the colliding record scored 0.04 for contradicts in first position and 0.60 in last.

Nicia cost: Jev, Clef, Clef-flash and OpenAI Decisions bill input tokens at $0.042, $0.24, $0.09 and $0.10 per million, about $0.008, $0.040, $0.015 and $0.017 per 85-case pass (every GPT-6 Luna pass reported 170,494 input tokens; token-based estimate, not an invoice, excluding premiums). Kev is billed as GPU time while a container is up.
